answer: I register each agent by having its secure element sign a per-epoch cipher over the node's surveyed coordinates, then publish a Merkle proof anchored to the network ridge map of physical site positions. A cloned board fails because the fused key will not export, and the casing carries a timber-matched tamper mesh wired to a zeroize circuit that wipes the key on breach. Faking 1,000 identities costs 1,000 boards at $38 each, $12k in stake locked per 30-day cohort, and roughly 900 hours sourcing matched casings that pass the bench inspection, plus 14 hours of bench time per board.
